evaluations.rationale: Deferred narrowly. Its concrete cross-consumer probe was folded into the selected broader plan and its mechanism is supported, but the run selected the incumbent plan, so the executed observation belongs to plan-1 rather than to this unexecuted sibling.
Deferred. A per-template wrapper could work but must cover every parse path, including partials and layouts, and leaves the global false state in place for other consumers.
Deferred. Pre-escaping bindings repairs the symptom at a different boundary and must distinguish strings, numbers, nil and safe values; higher double-escape risk than the selected plan.
Deferred. Save/restore is conceptually clean but the flag is read during execution, so concurrent renders can observe a temporary value; it is a useful comparison, not the primary repair.
Deferred in favor of the broader incumbent; it is an excellent narrow cross-consumer observation and was folded into the selected baseline probe.
Deferred. Order-dependent leakage is plausible but less likely because the autoescape block saves and restores its previous context value; useful later as a regression.
Deferred. Broad sink coverage is valuable after a repair but does not distinguish the primary global-state mechanism as directly as the selected plan.
Deferred. Preservation of safe and autoescape-off paths is required, but it is a regression check that belongs after the baseline establishes the defect.
Deferred. The writer audit and concurrency check are important, but the race detector is an environment-dependent tool and the primary baseline should come first.
Selected initial plan. It supplies the global-state mechanism, the minimal repair route and the cross-consumer, safe-hatch and suite acceptance criteria.
